referenceCamera.limitation: Generated reference camera is visually estimated; future fitting must not promote it to survey data.

objectClass.notes: Presentation-only reconstruction of the SFMOMA Botta facade and a restrained Snøhetta expansion glimpse. The generated concept is not surveyed architecture; authoritative footprint, world coordinates, collision, and portal identity remain outside this asset in the OSM world source.

reasoning: The silhouette combines several stepped brick volumes, a cylindrical turret, a tilted elliptical oculus, and a continuous compound-curved expansion shell.
Identity depends on nested macro, meso, and micro systems rather than a single facade mesh: brick wings contain entry, curtain-wall, podium, parapet, and relief subassemblies.
Seven visible repeated systems must remain independently controllable: brick courses, mortar joints, turret bands, oculus mullions, curtain-wall mullions, FRP ripples, and podium window openings.
Five visible material families plus dark metal mullions require separate PBR response and local overrides.
One generated front-three-quarter image leaves rear and roof geometry uncertain, so multiple orbit views and restrained inferred continuations are mandatory.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Ultra-complex is justified by the observed nested architectural hierarchy, compound curved shell, dense facade repetitions, multiple material zones, and identity-critical relief. The static use lowers articulation demand but not structural or review depth.

acceptedSingleViewLimitations: The generated reference is non-survey concept evidence; exact dimensions, brick modules, panel sizes, and oculus angle are not authoritative measurements.
Rear, roof, and camera-right hidden elevations will use restrained attached continuation and must be labeled inferred in review evidence.
The precise overlap between the Botta facade and Snøhetta expansion is approximate in this image.
OSM feature sf-building-41692824 remains the separate authority for footprint, coordinates, collision, and portal data; this reconstruction must not overwrite it.

detailInventory.note: Eighteen observed details are linked to exact future component.localFeatures or material.localOverrides keys. Spec authoring must create those keys or revise both artifacts together.

details.description: Alternating pale and charcoal horizontal stone courses wrap the cylindrical turret and converge around the oculus neck.
details.scale: meso, repeated courses approximately 1/24 of visible turret height
details.affects: turret identity, cylindrical depth, highlight rhythm, and long-range recognizability

details.description: The tilted elliptical oculus has a thick annular stone rim whose inner and outer chamfers catch separate highlight bands.
details.scale: meso annulus with bevel radius approximately 2 percent of oculus major axis
details.affects: oculus silhouette, rim thickness, attachment depth, and grazing-light readability

details.description: Dark radial and chord mullions subdivide the tilted elliptical glazing and visibly meet at the lower-central spine.
details.scale: micro-to-meso structural lines, legible at the fixed 1280 by 720 review view
details.affects: oculus identity, glass scale, and radial construction logic

details.description: Fine horizontal brick courses and recessed mortar lines repeat across every red facade mass without becoming a flat color fill.
details.scale: micro relief with course spacing approximately 1/110 of visible facade height
details.affects: material scale, surface depth, contact shading, and rejection of monolithic red boxes

details.description: The red facade resolves into multiple attached stepped wings and tower setbacks with distinct parapet heights rather than one rectangular slab.
details.affects: overall facade silhouette, depth ordering, and Botta massing identity

details.description: Large rectangular joints subdivide the charcoal granite podium into stone panels with darker crevice response.
details.affects: podium scale, stone construction, and cavity shading

details.description: The public entrance is a deep central void beneath projecting brick bars, with visible side reveals and contact shadow.
details.affects: grounding, public-entry readability, human scale, and front facade depth

details.description: Multiple dark-framed glass door leaves and transoms subdivide the central entrance opening.
details.affects: entrance scale, glazing depth, and walk-up readability

details.description: Narrow vertical glazed slots separate brick masses and use regular horizontal transoms to expose facade depth.
details.affects: brick-mass separation, vertical rhythm, and interior-depth cues

details.description: Closely spaced horizontal ripples follow the expansion's continuous convex, concave, and rounded corner profile.
details.scale: micro-to-meso repeated relief, approximately 1/90 of visible expansion height
details.affects: Snøhetta expansion identity, curved surface shading, and non-boxy continuity

details.description: A continuous blue-gray glazed ribbon with vertical mullions cuts horizontally through the white rippled expansion.
details.scale: macro horizontal aperture with meso mullion repetition
details.affects: expansion proportion, floor-scale cue, and continuity around rounded corners

details.description: Thin dark parapet caps trace the staggered upper edges of the brick wings and expose their separate depth planes.
details.affects: roofline silhouette, facade depth, and elevated-view legibility

details.description: Deeper horizontal shadow joints divide large brick bars and tower stages beyond the fine mortar-course relief.
details.affects: stepped volume readability and long-range horizontal cadence

details.description: A strong vertical dark channel descends from the oculus to the entry and interrupts the horizontal turret banding.
details.affects: turret orientation, oculus-to-entry alignment, and cylindrical band termination

details.description: Rows of small recessed rectangular window openings puncture the granite podium and reveal dark interior cavities.
details.affects: podium topology, facade cadence, and base-level depth

details.description: Cool glazing carries restrained low-roughness sky highlights while mullions and recessed interiors remain independently readable.
details.affects: glass-versus-stone separation, depth, and response under canonical daylight

details.description: Dark, shallow mortar joints separate individual brick units within each course without changing the macro silhouette.
details.affects: brick unit scale, cavity contrast, and close-view tactile response

details.description: Fine vertical and horizontal construction seams subdivide the pale rippled skin while preserving one contiguous curved facade.
details.affects: FRP construction scale, curvature continuity, and relief organization

definitionOfDone: At the fixed front-three-quarter review camera, the model reads as the intended SFMOMA concept through the broad stepped red-brick Botta facade, attached black-white banded turret, tilted elliptical oculus, deep entrance, and one contiguous pale rippled expansion.

At right, rear, left, and elevated orbit views, all inferred volumes remain grounded, attached, volumetric, and architecturally restrained; no facade-only planes, floating boxes, or disconnected relief are allowed.

Brick, granite, striped stone, glass, dark metal, and FRP use independent WebGPU-compatible PBR response with geometry or displacement for silhouette-relevant relief and no studio lighting baked into albedo.
Every one of the 18 inventoried identity details resolves to the exact named component.localFeatures or material.localOverrides key recorded in the inventory.
The model remains explicitly presentation-only: OSM feature sf-building-41692824 retains authority for footprint, EPSG:26910 coordinates, collision, and portal data.

featureGroups.name: Botta stepped brick massing and podium
qualityCriteria: Six or more attached macro masses preserve the asymmetric stepped roofline and the wide, low facade proportion visible in the reference.
The charcoal granite podium supports every front brick mass and is not represented as a floating dark strip.
Deep stage joints and thin parapet caps separate the brick volumes without fragmenting them into detached boxes.
failureModes: facade collapses to one rectangular red slab
stepped wings float or intersect without intentional overlap
granite base does not ground the brick masses

featureGroups.name: Striped cylindrical turret and tilted oculus
qualityCriteria: The striped cylindrical turret is embedded between the brick wings and remains the dominant identity feature.
At least six alternating bands remain clearly legible at 1280 by 720 and wrap the cylindrical form rather than reading as flat decals.
The thick elliptical oculus is tilted, socketed into the turret, beveled on both rims, and subdivided by radial/chord mullions.
failureModes: turret becomes a red chimney or generic cylinder
oculus is circular, untilted, flat, or floating
band rhythm disappears at the fixed review distance

featureGroups.name: Contiguous rippled expansion and glass ribbon
qualityCriteria: The pale rear expansion is one attached continuous shell with convex, concave, and rounded corner transitions.
Horizontal ripple relief follows the shell curvature and remains visible under neutral and grazing light.
The blue-gray glass ribbon and mullions continue around the curved elevation without separating the expansion into stacked floating boxes.
failureModes: expansion is approximated as disconnected white boxes
ripple relief ignores the curved profile or is only painted into albedo
hidden continuation invents unsupported towers or detached cantilevers

featureGroups.name: Entry, podium, and glazing as human-scale structure
qualityCriteria: The central entrance is physically recessed beneath attached brick and granite reveals and includes a readable door/transom grid.
Granite window punches are real cavities or sockets with dark interiors rather than black rectangles painted on the base.
Vertical curtain-wall slots, horizontal transoms, and interior backing provide facade depth and consistent human scale.
failureModes: entry is flush with the facade or too small to establish human scale
glazing reads as opaque blue panels without mullion or interior separation

featureGroups.name: PBR relief, canonical lighting, and source-truth boundary
qualityCriteria: Brick, granite, striped stone, glass, dark metal, and FRP define independent albedo, roughness, normal or displacement, and AO intent; no channel aliases another.
Brick courses, mortar, turret bands, FRP ripples, panel seams, and gloss overrides remain tied to inventory evidence and survive canonical daylight relighting.
Reference-matched, neutral, and grazing-light captures distinguish geometric relief from baked studio highlights.
No transform, dimension, footprint, collision, coordinate, or portal claim is promoted from the generated image; those remain owned by the OSM world source.
failureModes: facade reads as flat plastic or uses one averaged material
studio shadow or highlight pixels are baked into albedo
presentation geometry overwrites or is represented as authoritative OSM source geometry

visualDeltaChecks: fixed-view delta for broad stepped facade width-to-height, roofline stages, and deep entry negative space
turret delta for cylindrical depth, body ratio, band count and spacing, oculus ellipse tilt, rim thickness, and radial mullion placement
expansion delta for one continuous rippled shell, rounded corners, and glass-ribbon continuity
human-scale delta for entry doors, granite window punches, and vertical curtain-wall bays
material delta for independent brick, granite, striped stone, glass, metal, and FRP albedo/roughness/relief response
source-boundary delta confirming no generated-image measurement is promoted over OSM footprint, coordinates, collision, or portal truth

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

actionReadiness.contract: The generator-returned Group is the only whole-object transform container. Six real macro components attach directly to it; each child socket is parent-local and exactly matches the child transform. Zero-length attachment endpoints are generator-compatibility placeholders only, not measured attachment topology.

attachmentEndpointContract.socketTruth: Each parent actionProfile socket localPosition/localRotation equals the associated child's parent-local transform.

requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For static attached parts, use the parent-local socket and child transform as hierarchy truth; the equal localStart/localEnd pair exists only to prevent generator cylinder substitution.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: The AI-generated front-three-quarter image is a source-honest modeling concept, not a survey or exact photographic record.
Visible form and palette guide presentation geometry; hidden right, rear, left, and roof surfaces are conservative continuity inference.
OSM sf-building-41692824 remains authoritative for footprint, EPSG:26910 placement, collision, height/source status, and portal identity.
Single-image PBR extraction is a bounded look-development hypothesis requiring neutral and grazing-light review.

All nine repetition systems are deliberately codegen-disabled with executable count zero. Six need non-radial placement, while the three oculus systems need ellipse-conforming placement and clipping that the generic circular radial loop cannot provide; descriptive instance totals remain production intent for a subject-specific WebGPU-safe factory.

coordinateFrame.scaleReference: reference-relative ratios only; no generated-image dimension is surveyed or authoritative
coordinateFrame.transformContract: Top-level components are relative to the implicit returned Group; every child position and rotation is relative to its named parent pivot.

dominantCurves: continuous rounded expansion corners and horizontal ripples

repetitionSystems.blockedReason: The generic generator only emits radial repetition; 160 brick courses would become a circular ring instead of horizontal relief on the stepped facade.

requiredCustomPlacement.contract: Place 160 shallow horizontal course strips in component-local facade planes, clipped at windows, entry reveals, and the oculus opening.

repetitionSystems.distribution: Reference-relative horizontal facade-course intent; it is deliberately absent from generic codegen until facade-grid production placement exists.

repetitionSystems.blockedReason: The generic radial loop cannot express a staggered running-bond mortar grid on stepped planar facades.

requiredCustomPlacement.contract: Place 320 course-aligned mortar joints with alternating half-course offsets in local facade planes and clip them at architectural openings.

repetitionSystems.distribution: Course-aligned mortar intent; runtime material response remains authoritative until a custom running-bond geometry placement exists.
repetitionSystems.geometry: independent height field plus close-range relief

repetitionSystems.blockedReason: The generic radial loop would overlap 18 torus instances at one elevation instead of stacking horizontal courses along the turret axis.

requiredCustomPlacement.contract: Place 18 annular courses at distinct local-Y elevations around the embedded cylinder, preserving alternating dark and pale bands.

repetitionSystems.distribution: Eighteen wrapped horizontal courses remain production intent and are deliberately absent from generic codegen until stacked-axis placement exists.

repetitionSystems.blockedReason: The generic circular radial loop halves placement radius, cannot reach the glazing center reliably, and cannot clip spokes or chords to the tilted elliptical boundary.

requiredCustomPlacement.contract: Place 13 dark-metal mullions in oculus-local space from the center/spine to the true elliptical glazing boundary, with explicit clipping and inherited assembly tilt.

repetitionSystems.distribution: Radial and chord mullions clipped to the tilted ellipse.
repetitionSystems.geometry: thin dark-metal strips above inset glazing

repetitionSystems.blockedReason: The generic radial loop cannot place vertical mullions and transoms in rectilinear curtain-wall bays.

requiredCustomPlacement.contract: Place 46 local facade-frame members as vertical bays and restrained transoms, clipped to the glazing boundaries.

repetitionSystems.distribution: Visible vertical bays and restrained transoms remain production intent and are absent from generic codegen pending custom facade-grid placement.

repetitionSystems.blockedReason: The generic radial loop would overlap torus instances instead of following the continuous pale shell curvature.

requiredCustomPlacement.contract: Place 72 horizontal ridge sweeps along the expansion curve-sweep surface with continuous tangency and no floating boxes or rings.

repetitionSystems.distribution: Horizontal ridges following one continuous curved shell remain production intent and are absent from generic codegen pending custom curve-following placement.

repetitionSystems.blockedReason: The generic radial loop would arrange podium windows in a circle instead of linear facade bays with visible return depth.

requiredCustomPlacement.contract: Place 28 punched-window proxies in measured local facade rows, including return depth and corner-aware clipping.

repetitionSystems.distribution: Small punched openings with visible return depth remain production intent and are absent from generic codegen pending custom linear-bay placement.
repetitionSystems.geometry: framed void proxies with dark backing

repetitionSystems.blockedReason: The generic circular radial loop cannot conform light stripe wedges to the oculus rim's unequal local X/Y radii.

requiredCustomPlacement.contract: Place 12 light annular stripe segments along the true elliptical rim, interleaved at 15-degree phase with the dark segments and inheriting the assembly tilt once.

repetitionSystems.distribution: Alternating light radial wedges around the tilted annulus.

acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.
acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.

AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.

AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.

Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
